principle: Explicit user attribute > model stereotype/default. Motion must survive the clip, not just the first frame.
notes: must_obey=true means the prompt names the attribute explicitly and the model must follow it. default_behavior=true means the prompt is deliberately generic and we are measuring the model's unprompted default (stereotype check). needs='t2v' runs from text alone; 'i2v' requires a still from the image model; 's2v' requires a still plus audio. Video adds a failure class images do not have: an attribute can be correct in frame 1 and wrong by frame 120, so every case names what must hold ACROSS the clip.
seed_policy: Wave 0 runs 1 seed for triage. default_behavior cases and any case that moves in wave 1 get 3 seeds before any conclusion is recorded. Motion is noisier per seed than a still image; a single-seed video result is an anecdote. Cases owned by beenga-image are not re-run here after wave 1 — they were measured to establish the base-model choice and that job is done.

cases.prompt: A 25-year-old Indian woman dancing casually in her living room, natural relaxed movement, realistic video.
cases.common_failure: Renders classical Bharatanatyam/Kathak hand positions, a performance stage, or ceremonial costume.
cases.across_clip: Movement stays casual for the whole clip rather than settling into a classical pose.

cases.prompt: A 27-year-old Indian man clapping his hands in time with music, medium shot, realistic video.
cases.common_failure: Fingers merge, multiply, or dissolve at the moment the hands meet.
cases.across_clip: Hand topology is stable through every contact event, not only at rest.

cases.prompt: A 30-year-old Indian woman walking down a modern street, side view, full body from head to feet in frame for the whole shot, steady camera tracking alongside her, realistic video.
cases.common_failure: Feet slide or skate, legs swap, stride length changes mid-clip.
cases.across_clip: Gait cycle is physically consistent from first step to last.
cases.rewrite_note: Rewritten 2026-08-16. The original never guaranteed feet in frame. Side view and full-body framing are now stated, because a gait cycle cannot be judged without seeing the feet. NOTE: this case still needs a per-frame foot-tracking instrument; sampled frames cannot answer it even with correct framing.

cases.prompt: Close-up of a 26-year-old Indian woman singing, medium shot, natural expression, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: A single sustained 'aa' vowel held for two seconds. Speech-trained lip-sync models almost never see a mouth held in one open shape for 40+ frames. This is the sharpest single probe in the suite.
desired_attributes: mouth stays open for the full vowel
cases.common_failure: Mouth closes and reopens repeatedly, treating a held vowel as a sequence of syllables.
cases.across_clip: Mouth aperture is stable for the duration of the vowel.

cases.prompt: Close-up of a 26-year-old Indian woman singing energetically, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: A fast Hindi lyric line, roughly 6 syllables per second.
desired_attributes: mouth keeps up with syllable rate
cases.common_failure: Mouth blurs into generic flapping; syllable boundaries are lost.
cases.across_clip: Articulation rate tracks the audio for the whole line.

cases.prompt: Close-up of a 30-year-old Indian man singing, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: A Hindi line dense in retroflex stops. These are underweighted in the English talking-head corpora (HDTF, VoxCeleb2) that supervise LatentSync and MuseTalk.
cases.common_failure: Collapses to the nearest English viseme. This is the direct test of whether the English-supervised viseme mapping transfers to Hindi.
cases.across_clip: Consonant articulation is visible, not smoothed away.

cases.prompt: Close-up of a 26-year-old Indian woman singing, realistic video.

desired_attributes: visible aspiration burst on the plosives
cases.common_failure: Aspirated and unaspirated pairs render identically.
cases.across_clip: Plosive articulation is present throughout.

cases.prompt: A 26-year-old Indian woman singing and moving to the rhythm of the song, medium shot, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: Four bars with a clear beat.
desired_attributes: body movement aligned to the beat
cases.common_failure: In arms A and B the body motion is generated with no access to the audio, so it cannot be on the beat — only the mouth is repaired. This case is designed to separate arm C from A and B, and is the reason arm C is in the bake-off at all.
cases.across_clip: Movement stays on the beat for all four bars.

cases.prompt: Close-up of a 26-year-old Indian woman singing, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: 2.5s of sung vocal followed by 2.5s of TRUE digital silence. Demucs vocal stems are not silent in their gaps — they sit around -62dB — so this probe uses synthesised silence to separate 'responds to bleed' from 'responds to music'.
desired_attributes: mouth stops moving when the vocal stops
mouth is at rest during silence
cases.common_failure: Mouth keeps articulating through the silent half. Observed by Biren on the first arm C reel: 'when simply music was in the end, still mouth movement was there.'
cases.across_clip: Articulation is present in the first half and absent in the second.

cases.prompt: Close-up of a 26-year-old Indian woman singing, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: 2.5s of sung vocal followed by 2.5s of the SAME song's instrumental stem, no vocal. This is the reported failure reproduced under control.
desired_attributes: mouth stops when the vocal stops
instrumental passage does not drive articulation
cases.common_failure: Mouth keeps singing over the instrumental. Fatal for a music video, where every song has an intro, a break and an outro with no vocal.
cases.across_clip: Articulation present in the first half, absent in the second.

cases.prompt: A 26-year-old Indian woman standing still and listening quietly, lips closed and relaxed, calm neutral expression, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: IDENTICAL audio to VID-SING-009. The only variable is the prompt, which no longer says 'singing'.
cases.common_failure: Control for VID-SING-009/010. Those kept mouthing through silence AND through instrumental, but their prompt said 'singing' — so the articulation may be prompt-driven rather than audio-driven. If the mouth goes still here, the prompt is the lever and per-segment prompting fixes it cheaply. If it keeps moving, S2V animates a mouth regardless of both prompt and audio, and the fix is architectural: VAD-segment the song and only run S2V over vocal-active spans.
cases.across_clip: Lips remain closed for the whole clip.

cases.prompt: A 26-year-old Indian woman standing quietly, calm neutral expression, realistic video.
cases.audio_notes: Five seconds of total digital silence. This is a CONTROL, not a test: it establishes the floor value of mouth_activity for this pipeline. Without it the 0.6 'stopped' threshold used on VID-SING-009/010/011 is an arbitrary number, and the arm C finding is directional rather than measured.
cases.common_failure: n/a — this is the reference the other three are scored against.
cases.across_clip: Whatever it does is the baseline.

cases.prompt: An Indian classical dancer performing bharatanatyam, holding precise hand mudras with fingers in exact positions, araimandi half-sitting stance, realistic video.
desired_attributes: mudra finger positions are precise and held
hands do not collapse into generic gestures
cases.common_failure: Fingers blur into generic dance hands; the codified mudra shape is approximated rather than held. A Western-weighted motion corpus has little bharatanatyam in it.
cases.across_clip: Mudra shape holds for the duration rather than decaying into a loose hand.
cases.why: Probing the one remaining candidate for a defect that is BOTH video-specific and India-specific. Every India-specific defect found so far has been appearance, which belongs to beenga-image. If a training target exists for this repo, it is most likely here.

Now constructed: a verified-loud vocal head (-15.8dB mean) shared with VID-SING-014, then 2.5s of the RAW Demucs gap (-61.1dB mean, -43.7dB peak).

cases.common_failure: Control for VID-SING-014. Establishes what the ungated stem does.
cases.across_clip: Articulation present in the first half, ideally absent in the second.

cases.audio_notes: REBUILT 2026-08-16. IDENTICAL loud vocal head to VID-SING-013. The only difference is the tail, gated by scripts/gate-vocal.mjs at -28dB to -91dB flat — true digital silence. One variable.
desired_attributes: mouth stops when the vocal stops
cases.common_failure: If this stops and VID-SING-013 does not, gating the stem is the fix for the music-drives-the-mouth defect and no pipeline restructuring is needed.

ownership: Production shots start from a reference still and run through i2v/s2v, so the still decides WHO the person is and WHAT they are wearing, and the video model decides what happens after frame 1. Appearance defects (ceremonial default, garment, complexion) are therefore beenga-image's to fix, on stills, where a sample costs $0.001 instead of $0.05. This suite owns the temporal failures that have no still-image equivalent: motion integrity, cloth and hair dynamics, attribute decay across a clip, lip-sync, and long-form joins. Added 2026-08-16: an indian_dance category, probing whether India-specific MOTION and garment-physics defects exist. This is the last candidate for a video-side training target.
